title: EastWest Dream Run 2026 Iloilo Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: EastWest Dream Run Iloilo 2026 Review: Field, Pace, Fees, Rules
meta_description: EastWest Dream Run Iloilo 2026 review: the Atria Park District 21 km, 10 km, 5 km and dog run, a 2:37 median half-marathon time, winning times, fees, finisher items and what was never published.
dek: What the EastWest Dream Run's Iloilo leg on 20 September 2026 was like: the course past Jaro and the river, the rules, how fast the field ran, what it cost, and what the race pages left out.
verdict: Enter if you live in or near Iloilo and want an unhurried, family-friendly city half marathon, or a 10 km, 5 km or dog run the whole household can do. The 2026 Iloilo leg drew more than 2,000 people to Atria Park District; the full results list 434 in the 21 km, a third of them women, with a median time of 2:37:39 and finishers out to 3:40. Two elite runners won in 1:14:09 and 1:33:17, but only nine runners broke 1:40. The catch is how little was published: no route map, start times or cut-offs appeared on the race pages. Ask RUNRIO for the race guide before you commit.

sections.heading: The Course: From Atria Past Jaro and the River
paragraphs: The Iloilo leg started and finished at Atria Park District [1]. The route went through the centre of Iloilo City, past the Jaro Cathedral belfry and along the riverfront [2]. The organiser describes it as running on broad, well-maintained roads and modern urban corridors [1].

No route map, elevation profile or aid-station plan was on the race pages. The series FAQ says there are aid stations along the route with water at the hydration stations, that parts of the route are closed to traffic, and that the road advisory is in the race guide [3]. The courses are measured to RUNRIO's own standards [4]; no certification is claimed. Walkers are asked to keep to the right so faster runners can pass [3].

sections.heading: Start, Cut-offs and Rules
paragraphs: The Race Roster listing gives the event as starting at 3am [5]; the start times for each distance were not published on the pages read. Nor were the cut-offs. The rules say courses close after the designated cut-off times, and the FAQ says an ambulance picks up everyone still on the course by the last cut-off and takes them to the finish [4][3]. In 2026 the slowest 21 km time in the results is 3:40:21 [6].

You must start within 15 minutes of your flag-off or be disqualified, and winners are decided on gun time [4]. The timing chip is on the back of the bib, so do not fold it or cover it [4]. Unofficial pacers are not allowed, and anyone who lets someone else wear their bib is disqualified and suspended from later RUNRIO races [4]. The 21 km is for runners 18 and over, the 10 km 16 and over and the 5 km 12 and over; each 3 km group of four needs at least one adult [4].

RUNRIO can delay, cancel or suspend a race for bad weather [4]. The Clark leg of the same series, set for 30 August 2026, was postponed because of the weather [7]; the organiser's release called Iloilo the second leg of a four-leg series [2].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Rogen Aguirre won the 21 km in 1:14:09, ahead of Marbert Celiz in 1:15:07 and Joshua Rey Javellana in 1:20:28 [6]. Jennylyn Nobleza won the women's race in 1:33:17, sixteen minutes clear of Ivy Ibañez in 1:49:29 [6]. Both winners were among the returning Team 7-Eleven qualifiers sent to the Borneo International Marathon in May 2026 [8], and Nobleza was second in the marathon at the 2025 National MILO Marathon Finals in Iloilo, in 3:16:08 [9].

Behind them the field is relaxed. Tenth place was 1:40:34 for men and 2:12:21 for women; only nine runners broke 1:40 and 48 broke two hours [6]. The median 21 km time was 2:37:39, 316 of the 406 timed runners finished inside three hours, and 14 took longer than 3:30 [6]. A third of the 434 runners listed in the 21 km were women [6].
The 10 km was won in 33:42 by Stephine Delariarte and in 49:04 by Marjorie Basea; 52 runners broke an hour and the median was 1:20:24 [6].

sections.heading: Field Size and Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: The organiser put the crowd at more than 2,000 runners, families and friends, aged from seven to 72 [2]. The results list 1,667 names: 434 in the 21 km, 563 in the 10 km, 581 in the 5 km, 66 in the 3 km and 23 in the dog run [6]. A nine-year-old finished second in the women's 3 km [2].

The 21 km cost P1,800 at the early-bird rate and P2,000 at the regular rate; the 10 km P1,200 and P1,400; the 5 km and the dog run P1,000 and P1,200; and the 3 km for a group of four P4,500 at the regular rate [5][4]. EastWest credit card holders could get a P500 rebate with a minimum spend of P3,000, and a group signing up ten runners got an eleventh place free [5]. Entries cannot be refunded, deferred or transferred, and you cannot change category once registered [4][3].

Every entrant gets a race singlet and bib [5]. Every finisher gets a medal, a loot bag and a finisher's towel; 21 km finishers also get a finisher's shirt, and dog-run entrants a dog bandana [3][5]. In the dog run the owner must be 18 or over, the dog at least six months old and on a leash throughout [4][3]. There is a baggage deposit, and changing areas and portable toilets in the activity area [3]. The organiser promised a post-race recovery lounge with massage and yoga [1], and runners found partner booths, games and giveaways [2].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you live in or near Iloilo and want a first or easy half marathon among runners of every speed, or a morning out for the family and the dog. The 21 km median of 2:37:39 and finishers out past 3:30 mean you will not be alone at the back.

Think twice if you want to race for a place against a deep field, if you need to see the route and cut-offs before you enter, or if you want a cheaper half marathon: the regular 21 km entry was P2,000.
A 2027 Iloilo leg has not been announced. The 2026 series moved on to Cagayan de Oro on 18 October [2].
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race pages, rules and FAQ, the full published results, and local reporting.

faqs.question: How fast is the EastWest Dream Run Iloilo half marathon?
faqs.answer: Fast at the front, relaxed behind. In 2026 the 21 km was won in 1:14:09 by Rogen Aguirre and 1:33:17 by Jennylyn Nobleza, both elite runners. Tenth place was 1:40:34 for men and 2:12:21 for women, the median time was 2:37:39, and the slowest listed finisher ran 3:40:21.

faqs.question: Is the EastWest Dream Run Iloilo good for a first half marathon?
faqs.answer: Yes, on the 2026 evidence. The median 21 km time was 2:37:39, 14 runners took longer than 3:30, and the slowest listed time was 3:40:21. The catch is that no cut-off was published on the race pages, so ask RUNRIO for the race guide. The 21 km is for runners aged 18 and over.

faqs.question: How much does the EastWest Dream Run Iloilo cost?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the 21 km cost P1,800 early bird or P2,000 regular, the 10 km P1,200 or P1,400, the 5 km and the dog run P1,000 or P1,200, and a 3 km group of four P4,500 regular. EastWest credit card holders could get a P500 rebate. Entries cannot be refunded, deferred or transferred.

faqs.question: What do finishers get at the EastWest Dream Run Iloilo?
faqs.answer: Every finisher gets a finisher's medal, a loot bag and a finisher's towel, on top of the race singlet and bib. Finishers of the 21 km also get a finisher's shirt, and dog-run entrants get a dog bandana. In 2026 there were also partner booths, games and giveaways after the race.

faqs.question: Can you run with your dog at the EastWest Dream Run Iloilo?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the 1 km dog run. The owner must be 18 or over, the dog at least six months old, and it must stay on a leash throughout. A second person can run with the dog if registered in another category. In 2026 the entry was P1,000 early bird, and 23 dog-run entries are listed in the results.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 about the 2026 Iloilo leg, run on 20 September 2026 at Atria Park District. Replaces a short review built on the organiser's release alone. Field counts, the median and the top-ten times are computed from the full Race Roster results. No weather section: Iloilo International Airport has no observations in the public METAR archive for race morning, and more distant stations are not used. No race-day air-quality reading could be read (the Inquirer report was blocked). No route map, start times, cut-offs or road advisory was published on the pages read, and no news report or runner account beyond the organiser's release was found. The release calls Iloilo the second leg; a pre-race release called it the third; the Clark leg had been postponed. The 3 km group early-bird fee is P4,000 on the graphic and P4,100 in the mechanics, so only the regular fee is given. No rating.
